ActiveDefault.description:
One setting this server turns on even when the run would have fitted without
it.

The list is the *whole* of what invariant 4 now permits without an opt-in: a
degradation not named here is still a 422 that asks for `allow`.

client_can_disable.description: Always true: one `params` field turns it off.

condition.description: When it is applied, in one sentence.

cost.description: What the run pays for it.

degrades.description: Whether leaving it on changes *what* is computed rather than how fast.

paths.description: The dotted paths it moves. Setting any of them in `params` pins it.

warning.description: The `plan.warnings` code this default raises, when it raises one.

drop_degenerate_groups.description:
Drop groups the judge scored identically across every member; see
[`AgentGrpoConfig::drop_degenerate_groups`].

end_on_no_tool_call.description:
`false` turns a turn that named no tool into an error observation
instead of the end of the trajectory; see
[`RolloutLimits::end_on_no_tool_call`]. Leave it alone for a run whose
policy answers, set it for a world that decides when the episode is
over.

environment.description:
One stateful environment per trajectory - HTTP, container or (explicitly)
the host.

epochs_per_update.description:
Optimizer passes over one update's rollouts. Spelled in full because
`training.epochs` is a different quantity - passes over an SFT dataset.

judge.description:
An addition, not a default. Absent, the environment's own reward is the
only one - which is the whole configuration of a verifiable task.

max_failed_turns.description:
Consecutive turns without a valid tool call before the trajectory is
cut as a truncation; see [`RolloutLimits::max_failed_turns`]. Zero
never cuts.

max_new_tokens_per_turn.description:
Generation budget for one assistant turn. `[grpo.sampling]`'s
`max_new_tokens` is the single-turn equivalent; the two live in
different sections because a turn is not a completion.

mcp_servers.description:
Tools served over MCP. With an environment, every server must be
explicitly declared stateless before it may be shared across members.

skip_empty_updates.description:
Skip an update left with fewer than two trainable trajectories rather
than failing the run; see [`AgentGrpoConfig::skip_empty_updates`].

system_suffix.description: Text appended to training and held-out system turns; creates a turn if absent.

template_variables.description:
Chat-template variables, e.g. `template_variables = { enable_thinking = false }`.
The runtime rejects `messages`, `tools`, `bos_token`, `eos_token` and
`add_generation_prompt`, which are supplied by the renderer.

Allow.description:
A degradation the caller explicitly accepts.

Each of these changes *what* is computed, not only how fast, and neither is
recoverable from a warning: both lose data outright. The resolver never
reaches for one on its own; without the opt-in it fails and says what it
would have done.

`fast_generation` and `kv_f16` are handled as defaults rather than
degradations: neither discards data, and the runtime may fall back to F32
after probing the device. `kv_f16_may_fall_back` records that the estimate
may therefore overstate the saving.

AppliedRule.description: The net configuration move made by one rule.

ArtifactEntry.description:
One artefact of a run, by a fixed name rather than by path.

The name is what `GET /v1/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name}` takes. Naming the
members of a closed inventory is what keeps the download route from being a
path parameter - and therefore from being an arbitrary file reader.

downloadable.description:
Whether `GET.../artifacts/{name}` will serve the bytes. False for a
directory, and for a file over the download limit.

present.description:
Whether it is on disk right now. A run that has not finished has no
adapter yet, and that is worth saying rather than omitting.

baseline_bytes.description: Already in use before this process allocated anything.

capped.description: The request was above the server-wide budget and was lowered to it.

effective_bytes.description: `min(requested, ceiling, total) − baseline − margin`, floored at zero.

margin_bytes.description: Reserve for fragmentation and unmodelled allocations.

requested.description: The request as the operator wrote it: `"all"`, `"6GiB"`, or `"0.8"`.

total_bytes.description: Absent when the platform does not report a total for this budget.

BudgetRequest.description: 'all', a byte count ('6GiB', 4096), or a fraction of the total (0.8)

Budgets.description: The pair of budgets a resolution is checked against.

unified.description:
Device and host memory are one pool, so the two budgets above describe
the *same* bytes and the check is made against the smaller of them.
Treating them as independent would let the resolver promise the
model twice.

checkpoint.description:
Write a checkpoint before stopping. Only meaningful with
`at: "boundary"`; asking for it with `at: "now"` is refused rather than
silently dropped, because there is no resumable point between two
boundaries and a client that thought it had a checkpoint would not.

unified_memory.description:
True when device and host memory are the same physical pool (Metal,
iGPU). Two independent budgets would then double-count the model.

CheckpointDtype.description:
Storage precision for the layer outputs retained by gradient checkpointing.

A 16-bit checkpoint halves that term, and would halve the host-transfer traffic
if activation offloading were combined with it. It is opt-in, and not merely
because it breaks bit-parity: measurement on the CPU fixture shows a 16-bit
checkpoint perturbs the LoRA update by roughly its own relative precision
(~1e-3), which is about four orders of magnitude more than the F32 recompute's
reassociation error. Neither F16 nor BF16 was clearly better at that scale. So
this trades a real amount of gradient fidelity for memory - appropriate when a
run would not otherwise fit, not a free win.

CheckpointEntry.description:
One checkpoint found on disk.

A directory read, not a run's memory: a run restored from the state directory
lists its checkpoints exactly like a live one, and a checkpoint deleted by
hand disappears from the listing without anything having to be told.

adapter.description: The adapter GGUF exported beside the state directory, when it is there.

bytes.description: Total size of the state directory.

complete.description:
False for a directory whose manifest is missing or of another format
version: it is listed rather than hidden, because a client that asked to
resume from it deserves to know why it cannot.

written_at.description: Unix seconds of the manifest, i.e. when the checkpoint was published.

directory.description:
Absent when the run writes no checkpoints, which is not the same as an
empty directory.

latest.description: The id a resume would pick, i.e. what `fork_from` resolves to by default.

mode.description:
`steps` | `best_eval` | `steps_and_best_eval`, the same vocabulary the
configuration document uses.

CollectApiConfig.description:
An OpenAI-compatible endpoint that stands in for the policy while a
collection runs: the teacher a warm-start dataset is distilled from when no
local model is strong enough. The key is read from `api_key_env`, never
from the document.

temperature.description: Sent when set; the provider's default otherwise.

CommandAccepted.description:
What every control route answers.

One shape for pause, resume, cancel, checkpoint and patch, because a client
scripting them wants one thing to read: what the run is now, and when what it
asked for lands.

applied.description: The dotted paths a `PATCH` accepted, in a fixed order. Empty elsewhere.

applies_at_iteration.description:
The iteration the request takes effect at - the next one, since a run is
only interruptible at its progress callback. Absent when the effect
was immediate, as for a run cancelled before it ever started.

ConfigDocument.description:
The configuration *document*: the exact schema of the CLI's TOML file.

Public because it is the one schema three frontends share: the CLI reads it
from TOML, the server accepts it as JSON, and the resolver renders its own
output back through it. The resolver builds one of these instead of a
[`RunConfig`](crate::RunConfig) directly, so that "the resolver cannot
produce a config the CLI would refuse" holds *by construction*: the only way
from a document to a `RunConfig` is [`build`](crate::build()), which is what
`load` calls.

[`RunConfig`](crate::RunConfig), by contrast, stays internal: it is the
engine's shape and changes at the engine's pace.

oneOf.description:
`[lora]`: required by `lora` and `hybrid`, refused by `full` and
`partial`. Optional as a *document* section because a run that trains
base tensors has no adapter at all, and demanding rank, alpha and
targets from it would be demanding the shape of something it does not
create.

`[optimizer.<name>]`: the chosen optimizer's own knobs. A table for an
optimizer the run did not choose is refused at build time.

`[output]`: where the run's result goes, and which kind of result it is.
The kind is defaulted from the policy when absent; the path is not, so
a document that names no output is refused.

`[reference]`: the frozen model a KL penalty is scored against. Its own
section rather than a field of `[ppo]` or `[grpo]`, because one file
serves every objective that declares a KL term.

`[trainable]`: which base tensors a `partial` or `hybrid` run selects.
Absent for `lora`, and refused when present alongside it - a selector a
policy ignores is a selector the user believes is in effect.

Conversation.description: A trajectory: the messages the policy and its tools exchanged.

metadata.description: The entries that differ from the scenario's.

prefix.description: The messages start after the scenario's own prefix.

DataSpec.description:
Where the training data is: a literal path, or a dataset id from
`POST /v1/datasets` - mutually exclusive.

`dataset` is an id and nothing else, the same shape as [`RewardRef`] and
[`JudgeRef`]: this crate never touches a filesystem or a store, so
resolving it to bytes is entirely the server's job (`resolve::plan_recipe`
turns it into a real `path` before this recipe ever reaches [`crate::resolve`]).

format.description:
`auto` | `text` | `jsonl`. Absent is `auto`. Ignored when `dataset` is
set - a stored dataset already knows its own format.

path.description:
A literal filesystem path. The server accepts it only when its
`allow_local_paths` setting is on (default: loopback only).

DatasetPreview.description:
`GET /v1/datasets/{id}/preview`

Examples exactly as they are read off disk: a `chat-jsonl` or
`preference-jsonl` dataset answers parsed JSON objects, a `text` dataset
answers raw lines - never
re-formatted, since the point of a preview is to show what training would
actually see.

DatasetStatsView.description:
Length statistics as they ride along a dataset's own card - the flattened
view of `retrograd_plan::DatasetStats` a client reads without fetching a
plan.

measured.description:
False when these came from the character heuristic rather than a real
tokenizer - true once `POST /v1/datasets/{id}/tokenize` has run.

DatasetTokenization.description:
`POST /v1/datasets/{id}/tokenize` - the measured lengths, and what they mean
for a context you have not chosen yet.

stats.description: `measured` is `true` here by construction - a real tokenizer ran.

tokenizer.description:
The cache key these lengths were stored under: the vocabulary and chat
template that produced them, not the file that carried them. Every model
answering the same key reuses this measurement.

truncation.description:
The share of examples that would be truncated at each of a few common
contexts, keyed by the context as a decimal string.

DatasetView.description:
`POST /v1/datasets` and `GET /v1/datasets/{id}`.

`id = "ds_" + sha256(content)`: two uploads of the same bytes answer the
same card, which is where the idempotence of `POST /v1/datasets` comes
from.

DerivedField.description:
One field the resolver decides when `params` leaves it out, and the rule it
decides it with.

This is what replaced `GET /v1/presets`. A profile was a word the server had
to interpret; this is the interpretation itself, published - a client that
wants its own "fast" or "thorough" builds one out of these rules and sends it
as `params`.

applies_to.description:
`any` | `sft` | `grpo` | `ppo` | `rollout` | `evaluation` | `checkpoint`:
when the rule applies at all.

client_can_set.description:
Always true, and stated rather than implied: every one of these is a
`params` field a client may set instead.

path.description:
Dotted field path, the same grammar as `params`, `provenance` keys and
the `PATCH` whitelist. One path grammar for the whole API.

thresholds.description:
The numbers in that sentence, named. A `BTreeMap` so the bytes are
deterministic.

DeviceInfo.description: One ggml device visible to this build.

total_bytes.description:
Absent when the backend does not report a memory budget, which is not
the same as reporting zero.

DistillToml.description:
`[distill]`. Every key that has a sensible value without being written has
one: a distillation run is described by a teacher, a prompt file and a
budget, and the rest is tuning.

data.description: Offline mode only: the chat JSONL the sidecar describes.

offline_epochs.description: Offline mode only: passes over the corpus.

prompts.description:
On-policy mode only. Optional in the schema and required by
`build_distill` for that mode, rather than required here: an offline
document has no prompt file, no update count and no sampler, and forcing
it to write three ignored keys is how a reader ends up believing they
mean something.

oneOf.description: On-policy mode only, same reasoning as `prompts`.

DownloadLink.description:
`POST /v1/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name}/link`: a download a browser can
navigate to without a token.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds after which the link is refused.

href.description: Same-origin path, query included. Good for this one artefact only.

DynamicSampling.description:
DAPO dynamic sampling: after the group baseline drops zero-signal groups,
keep drawing replacement prompts (continuing the round-robin) until the
update carries `prompts_per_update` informative groups, or the candidate
budget `prompts_per_update * max_resample_factor` is exhausted. Keeps the
effective batch full as the policy converges.

max_resample_factor.description:
Cap on candidate groups per update, as a multiple of
`prompts_per_update`. Must be at least 2 (1 would allow no resampling).

EnvironmentEntry.description:
A declared environment. No image, no limits, no mount: the operator chose
those, and publishing them would be one step from letting a client choose
them.

tools.description:
Empty for an `http` environment, whose tool list belongs to its own
server rather than to this catalogue.

ErrorCode.description:
The closed vocabulary a client's `match` is written against.

`message` and `hint` are prose and may be reworded release to release;
`code` is the part of the contract, tested (`tests/error_catalog.rs`)
against `ERRORS.md`.

The spelling beside each variant is the one serde writes *and* the one
`as_str()` returns - one token, so the two cannot drift and no test has
to check them against each other.

`rename_all` is for the schema, which reads the container rule and not
the per-variant spelling; every spelling below is already snake case.

EvaluateRequest.description:
`POST /v1/runs/{id}/evaluate` - one evaluation out of schedule.

The whole request, and it is empty: an ad-hoc evaluation is the *configured*
evaluation, run now. A dataset here would be a different measurement wearing
the same name, and comparing it with the scheduled curve would be wrong.

EvaluationResult.description:
What an ad-hoc evaluation measured, and where the run was when it did.

This result is **not** part of the run's evaluation history: it does not move
`best`, does not count towards patience and never writes a `best` checkpoint.
A client that could feed the early-stopping state by asking questions could
end a run by polling it.

accuracy.description: Preference only: share of evaluation pairs ranked as preferred.

iteration.description:
The iteration the evaluation ran at, so it can be lined up against the
metric stream.

FeatureDtype.description:
Storage precision for the PPO critic's host-side feature matrix.

The critic keeps one row of `hidden_dim` features per completion state for the
whole update - predictions, GAE and `value_epochs` passes of full-batch Adam all
read the same matrix - so the buffer is `total_completion_states * hidden_dim`
and it lives in host RAM, not on the device. A 16-bit row halves it; the fit
still runs in F32, one chunk converted at a time, so the arithmetic is unchanged
and only the stored rows are rounded.

Opt-in, and the reason is the same one [`CheckpointDtype`] gives: rounding the
features perturbs the value regression. That perturbation is benign in a way the
gradient one is not - the baseline only reduces the variance of the policy
gradient and never biases the update - but "benign" is not "absent", and the
current default stays until a measurement asks for the memory back.

auth.description:
Requests need a bearer token. Informational: a client learns that it
needs one from the `401`, not from here.

mode.description:
`server` for the control plane; `viewer` for the read-only process of
`retrograd-server view`, which serves one run's trajectories and
nothing else.

ui.description: The web interface is served under `/`.

FieldError.description:
One field-level problem, located by a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the
request body.

hint.description:
What to do about it, only when there is a short, concrete answer. A
vague hint is worse than none.

ForkFrom.description:
Where a fork starts from.

Two shapes, and the difference is who supplies the configuration. `run` names
a run this server knows, so the parent's own effective configuration is
reused - that is the fork, and the resume. `path` names a checkpoint
directory, which carries a manifest and no configuration at all, so a `recipe`
or a `config` has to come with it.

checkpoint.description:
A checkpoint id under the parent's checkpoint directory (`step-400`,
`best`), or absent for the most recent one - the same resolution
`--resume` performs.

path.description:
A `.state` directory, for a checkpoint written by something other than
this server.

GefenToml.description:
`[optimizer.gefen]`. `variant` selects a slot table, so it moves the
layout version rather than appearing as a declared hyperparameter.

GenerateRequest.description: `POST /v1/runs/{id}/generate` - sample against the adapter as it is now.

chat.description:
Wrap the prompt in the model's chat template as one user turn. On by
default: an instruction-tuned adapter sampled without its template
answers as a text completer, which reads as a broken adapter rather than
as a missing flag.

include_base.description: Sample the same prompt again with the adapter disabled. Doubles the cost.

seed.description:
Sampling seed. Fixed by default, so two calls at the same step return the
same text and a difference is a difference in the weights.

base_text.description: Present only when `include_base` asked for it.

GroupSummary.description:
One group of an update. PPO has no groups: its rollouts are one group
whose `group` is absent, addressed as `-`.

reward_std.description:
Population standard deviation of the rewards. Zero means the group
carried no signal to learn from.

judge_weight.description:
Default weight of a verdict in the final reward. Required as soon as a
judge is declared: a judge that contributes an unstated amount to the
gradient is the one thing this section must not allow.

max_stalled_updates.description:
Consecutive zero-signal updates tolerated before the run stops; `0`
never stops. Defaults to `DEFAULT_MAX_STALLED_UPDATES`.

oneOf.description:
`"persistent"` (default) or `"oneshot"`. Persistent keeps one worker
alive for the whole loop behind a version handshake; a command that
reads its stdin to the end before answering needs `"oneshot"`.

reward_timeout_seconds.description:
Deadline of one reward batch, in seconds. Also covers the first batch's
worker startup in the persistent mode.

backends.description: Backends compiled into this build, e.g. `["cpu", "metal"]`.

status.description: Always `"ok"`: the endpoint is liveness, so a body at all is the answer.

JudgeEntry.description:
A judge declared by the operator. `client_settings` is the explicit list of
what a recipe may set on it: choices of method, with no side effect outside
the process. Endpoint, model and key are absent by design.

JudgeFailurePolicy.description: What a judge failure does to the update it happened in.

JudgeRef.description:
A judge reference plus the method settings a client may choose. The
endpoint, the model and the credential are the operator's and never appear.

KvDtype.description:
Storage precision requested for the differentiable training KV cache.
F16 is enabled only when the active device reports the differentiable Flash
Attention forward and backward ops for the model's head geometry; every
other device falls back explicitly to F32.

Limits.description: Per-run memory limits, capped by the server-wide budgets.

LoraDtype.description:
Storage precision for trainable LoRA A/B matrices. Gradients and optimizer
state remain F32 for both variants.

Deserializes from `"f32"` / `"f16"` so every TOML frontend spells it the
same way and none of them can silently drop the field.

MasterWeights.description:
Whether a half-precision base weight is trained through an F32 master copy.

Without one the update kernel reads the parameter, adds the step and rounds
the sum back onto the same grid, so a step below one ulp is a whole ulp
taken at random: the trajectory follows the rounding rather than the
gradient. That is what [`crate::MIN_BASE_STEP_ULPS`] refuses. A master copy
accumulates in F32 and writes the store through one cast, which makes those
rates trainable at four bytes per trained element.

McpServerEntry.description:
A declared MCP server, with the tools it really exposes after the
allow/deny filters. The catalogue connects at startup, so this list is
verified rather than declarative.

required.description:
A required server that fails to connect stops the server from starting;
an optional one is reported `skipped` and its tools are simply absent.

MemberDetail.description: One rollout with its text: a `completion`, or a `conversation`.

reward.description: What the optimizer was handed, after shaping.

tool_errors.description: Tool results that reported an error.

trained.description:
True once an `outcome` confirms it, false for an exclusion, absent
when the run stopped before saying.

turns.description: Assistant turns of a conversation; zero for a completion.

MemoryEstimate.description:
The estimate, one field per line item.

The names that also exist in [`MemoryReport`] are spelled identically, so
`estimated` and `measured` can be subtracted field by field instead of
aligned. The fields with no measured
counterpart (`dequant_scratch_bytes`, the activation/logit split, the host
lines) are the estimate's own detail.

attention_bytes.description:
The materialized attention scores. The optimizer context has no flash
attention on the differentiable path, so this term is real and grows
with `n_ctx`.

co_resident_bytes.description:
The models held beside this one for the whole run: a distillation
teacher, a fixed-reference anchor, or both. Separate from
`model_weight_bytes` so an estimate can be compared with a
`MemoryReport` byte by byte.

dequant_scratch_bytes.description:
Transient dequantization buffers the backend allocates for a quantized
weight. Several GiB have been observed on CUDA.

host_rollout_bytes.description: Rollout trajectories held for one update.

optimizer_state_bytes.description:
Persistent optimizer state of that set: `8N` for AdamW, `0` for SGD,
`4N` for a Muon-eligible matrix.

trainable_parameter_bytes.description:
The resolved trainable set - LoRA factors today. Named for the role
rather than for one policy, so a partial or hybrid estimate lands in the
same posts instead of inventing parallel ones.

trainable_parameters_are_model_subset.description:
Whether `trainable_parameter_bytes` is already inside
`model_weight_bytes`, i.e. selected out of the loaded weights rather
than allocated on top of them. The device rollup adds the parameters
only when this is false.

oneOf.description:
Filled by phase 4 (step 6). Absent means "not measured yet", which is not
the same as measured-at-zero.

tool_call_id.description: On a `tool` message: the call it answers.

MetricsPage.description:
`GET /v1/runs/{id}/metrics`

The pull half of the event stream: the same events, filtered to `metrics` and
served from the ring or `events.jsonl`. `next_since` is what to pass back to
continue, so polling is a loop with no bookkeeping on the client.

ModelFile.description: One GGUF file under the path roots.

root.description: The root it was found under.

roots.description:
The roots walked: the server's `path_roots`, or its working directory
when it declares none.

truncated.description: The walk stopped at its bound; some files are not listed.

ModelFileRole.description: What a GGUF file is for, judged by its name.

ModelGeometry.description:
Geometry of a model, as the resolver reads it. Exposed because a client that
wants to reason about its own budget needs the same numbers.

ModelToml.description:
`[model]` is optional as a *document* section because a frontend may supply
the base model itself - the CLI's `--model`/`--device`, a request field.
What is not optional is the resolved
[`RunConfig::model`](crate::RunConfig::model): [`build_with`](crate::build_with)
refuses a document whose path is neither written nor overridden.

fallback_learning_rate.description:
The rate the parameters Muon declines are updated at: its own value,
not a ratio of `training.lr`.

Objective.description: What the run is for. Selects the algorithm and the shape of phase 1.

enabled.description:
`false` turns the export off while keeping the table: how a client
declines an export the server would otherwise add. Absent means on.

reason.description:
One sentence, required for `derived` and `measured`. Absent for a value
that is simply the default or simply what the caller asked for - there is
nothing to explain.

OutputToml.description:
`[output]`: the run's result.

`path` is where it is written; `kind` is what it is. The two are separate
because they answer different questions and only the second can be wrong:
a `model` export of a hybrid run would silently drop the adapter, and an
`adapter` export of a full run would be an empty file.

OverlongPenalty.description:
DAPO soft overlong punishment: a progressive reward penalty over the last
`buffer_tokens` of the generation budget, applied before the group
baseline. Teaches the policy to conclude instead of merely ignoring
overruns (as `mask_truncated` does).

PatchRequest.description:
`PATCH /v1/runs/{id}` - the whitelist of the contract, and nothing else.

`deny_unknown_fields` is what makes the list closed: `n_ctx`, `lora`,
`algorithm` and every path are rejected by the deserializer before a handler
runs, and the handler turns that into the 409 that points at `fork_from`.
Field names follow the *document* grammar (`training.lr`), the same one
`params`, `provenance` and `GET /v1/defaults` speak.

PlanRequest.description:
`POST /v1/plan` and `POST /v1/runs`.

Exactly one of `recipe` (form (a): an intention) or `config` (form (b): a
complete configuration, the same schema as the CLI's TOML). Form (c) - a raw
TOML body - arrives as `config` too, parsed by the extractor.

oneOf.description:
A whole configuration document. Skips the semantic phases but not the
budget check.

Continue from a checkpoint. With `fork_from.run` this is the whole
body: the parent supplies the configuration and `params` go on top.

name.description: Human label. No uniqueness is imposed; identity is the run id.

params.description:
The client's own parameters: a partial document tree, spelled exactly as
the CLI's TOML spells it. Every leaf it sets is **locked** - no phase may
re-derive it - and everything it leaves out the server derives, from the
rules `GET /v1/defaults` publishes.

effective_config.description:
The effective configuration, in the same schema `config` takes on input.
Server-declared values are redacted to their catalogue id.

provenance.description: Flat map, keyed by dotted field path.

defaults_applied.description:
What phase 2bis turned on because it is better on this machine at this
context - not because the run was cornered. Disjoint from [`Self::levers`]
by construction: a setting phase 3 pushed further is a sacrifice and
appears there instead.

eval_truncation_fraction.description:
The same figure for the eval dataset, when there is one - an evaluation
that truncates 40% of its examples does not measure what it claims to,
and that is invisible unless it is reported next to the training figure
rather than folded into it.

iterations.description: Epochs for SFT, updates for PPO/GRPO.

levers.description: The levers phase 3 applied, in the order it applied them.

truncation_fraction.description:
Share of examples longer than the resolved context, rounded to four
decimals by [`reported_fraction`] so the payload carries no float the
caller cannot read.

PlanWarning.description:
One warning, with a code a client can match on.

A string alone was enough while every warning was advice for a human. It is
not enough now that one of them - `sampling_distribution_approximated` - is
how the API discharges its side of invariant 4: a client that has to *detect*
an approximation cannot be asked to grep prose.

code.description: Stable identifier, `snake_case`. Part of the contract.

field.description:
The dotted configuration path this warning is about, when there is one
field that is the reason for it. Absent for a
warning about the request as a whole.

message.description: One sentence for a human, and free to be reworded.

oneOf.description:
`"persistent"` (default) or `"oneshot"`. Persistent keeps one worker
alive for the whole loop behind a version handshake; a command that
reads its stdin to the end before answering needs `"oneshot"`.

reward_timeout_seconds.description:
Deadline of one reward batch, in seconds. Also covers the first batch's
worker startup in the persistent mode.

PreferenceToml.description:
`[preference]`. Everything but `data` has a default; the constant a loss
does not read is refused beside it.

beta.description: Defaults per loss: 0.1 for dpo, ipo and orpo, 2.0 for simpo.

logps_drop_warn.description: In nats, greater than zero. Defaults to 2.0.

reference.description:
dpo and ipo: `initial` (the default) or `base`. Absent when
`[reference]` declares the anchor.

targets.description:
LoRA target shorthands or patterns, as the CLI's `--targets` accepts.
Absent selects the architecture's automatic profile.

allOf.description:
Flattened so the HTTP response is the versioned engine contract itself,
not an envelope carrying a second schema.

Problem.description:
Wire shape of a problem document (RFC 9457). Serialized by hand rather than
derived from `ApiError` so the field order - and therefore the bytes - is
fixed. Published as the `Problem` component: every failure of the API but
the OpenAI routes' has this body.

meta.description:
The payload specific to the problem type, e.g. the dominant memory
posts of `insufficient-memory`.

trace_id.description: The id every log line of this request carries.

type.description:
`https://retrograd.dev/problems/<slug>`: the slug is what a client
branches on.

PromptView.description: A prompt, whole or cut to a preview.

cut.description: True when a message was cut to `preview_chars`.

Provenance.description:
The provenance map. `BTreeMap` so the serialized bytes are the same for two
identical resolutions (invariant 3).

allow.description:
Opt-ins for the degradations of invariant 4. Deduplicated and sorted on
validation, so two spellings of the same set resolve identically.

output.description:
Where the adapter and the checkpoints go. Defaulted by the caller (the
server derives them from its state directory), never guessed here.

seed.description:
Seed for the LoRA initialisation and the samplers. A run created without
one must still get one recorded, or a fork is not reproducible.

ReferenceToml.description:
`[reference]`: the anchor, and the width it runs at.

The anchor's precision is the one in its file: a quantization key here
would make the scores depend on a setting rather than on the model the
path names.

ctx.description: Context width of the anchor. Absent follows `[training].ctx`.

device_peak_bytes.description: Common persistent allocations plus the larger mutually-exclusive phase.

RewardEntry.description:
A reward declared by the operator. The command itself never leaves the
server.

mode.description:
How the trainer speaks to it: one worker for the run (`"persistent"`),
or one process per batch (`"oneshot"`). Listed because it changes
nothing a client sends and everything a client's timings look like.

The spelling of [`retrograd_core::RewardMode`] rather than the type: the
vocabulary is the trainer's, and publishing it as its own schema would
freeze a second copy of it here.

RewardMode.description:
How the reward command is spoken to.

The protocol on the wire is the same in both: one JSON request per line
in, one JSON response per line out, in order. What differs is the
lifetime of the process that speaks it - and with it, who pays the
command's startup.

`rename_all` is for the schema, which reads the container rule and not
the per-variant spelling; the spellings below are already lowercase.

RewardRef.description: A catalogue reference: an id and nothing else.

RunEvent.description:
One line of `events.jsonl`, and one SSE frame.

`seq` is monotonic per run and starts at 1, so `?since=0` replays everything
and a client can tell a gap from a duplicate.

RunEventPayload.description:
The event types the API lists.

`Metrics` is one of them because the API lists `metrics` among the SSE types
*and* gives it a pull route, and neither can be served from an event that
does not exist.

oneOf.description:
One emission of the metrics bus, the same values TensorBoard receives.
A `BTreeMap` so the bytes are stable, and non-finite values are absent
rather than `null`.

accuracy.description: Preference only: share of evaluation pairs ranked as preferred.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque: pass it back as `?cursor=` for the next page. Absent on the last
page, which is how a client knows to stop.

RunProgress.description:
Where a run has got to. Every figure comes from an observer event, so a field
is absent until the run has actually reported it once - never zero standing
in for unknown.

Non-finite measurements are stored as `None`, never rendered: `serde_json`
writes a `NaN` as `null`, which would be the one place in the API where
absence and nullity disagree. And the floats stay `f32` - the width the
engine reports them in, because widening one to `f64` writes a learning
rate of `2e-4` as `0.00019999999494757503`.

iterations.description:
What the plan said the run would do, so a client can render a fraction
without fetching the plan.

RunStatus.description:
The stable state vocabulary that clients may branch on. Runtime
transitions are documented on
[`crate::runtime::registry::transition_allowed`], which is also what
enforces them.

The spelling beside each variant is what serde writes and what `as_str()`
returns.

`rename_all` stays, and is not redundant: `utoipa` builds the schema's
`enum` from the variant identifiers and the *container* rule only - it
does not read the per-variant `rename` the macro emits. Without this
line the OpenAPI document would publish `"Queued"` while the API sends
`"queued"`, silently. `run_status_is_published_as_it_is_serialized`
checks the two renderers against each other.

RunSummary.description:
One entry of `GET /v1/runs`. Deliberately small: a listing is polled, and a
full configuration per run would make it expensive to poll.

created_at.description:
Unix seconds. Not RFC 3339: every other time in this API is a number,
and one format is easier to consume than two.

model.description: The base model's file name - not its path, which is the server's.

objective.description: The recipe objective, for a run created from a recipe.

queue_position.description: Rank in the device queue, from one, while the run is `queued`.

RunView.description:
`GET /v1/runs/{id}` and the `201` of `POST /v1/runs`.

The three heavy fields are carried as pre-rendered JSON. They are produced by
serializing the typed resolution once, at creation, and then written to the
journal and served verbatim - which is both cheaper than re-rendering and the
only way a run restored from disk answers the same bytes it answered while it
was alive.

holds_device.description:
Weights, KV caches and optimizer state stay allocated while a run is
paused. True whenever this run is holding the device.

ServerMode.description:
What kind of process answers. `rename_all` is kept for the same reason
as on [`RunStatus`]: the schema reads the container rule only.

shuffle.description:
Shuffle the training rows between epochs, seeded from `lora.seed`.
Defaults to `true`; set it to `false` to replay the file order.

template_variables.description:
Chat-template variables, e.g. `template_variables = { enable_thinking = false }`.
The runtime rejects `messages`, `tools`, `bos_token`, `eos_token` and
`add_generation_prompt`, which are supplied by the renderer.

Source.description: How a field got its value.

model.description:
The model whose tokenizer and chat template decide the lengths. Subject
to the same `path_roots` check as `recipe.model`.

ToolEntry.description: One tool as the policy will actually see it.

TrainableToml.description:
`[trainable]`: the base selection of a `partial` or `hybrid` run.

Every selector is off by default and an omitted `layers` means all blocks,
so an empty section selects nothing - which `build` refuses rather than
resolving to the empty set.

modules.description:
Module aliases (`"attn"`, `"ffn"`), individual stems (`"attn_q"`) or
explicit tensor patterns. Norms are not modules: they follow `norms`.

TrainingBudget.description: How much training to do. Exactly one key.

lr.description:
The base rate the schedule multiplies. Warm-up and decay keep their
shape around it.

gradient_accumulation.description:
Micro-batches accumulated before one optimizer step - TRL's
`gradient_accumulation_steps`. `micro_batch * gradient_accumulation` is
the token window one AdamW step trains, and it must divide `ctx`.
Optional on a rollout algorithm, where it is pinned to
`ctx / micro_batch` (one step never spans less than a whole rollout).

oneOf.description:
Train half-precision base weights through an F32 master copy:
`"auto"` (default), `"f32"` or `"off"`.

max_gpu_duty_cycle.description:
Upper target for the fraction of wall time this trainer spends waiting
on GPU work it submitted, so a neighbouring workload gets regular
compute windows. Finite, in `(0, 1]`; `1.0` is the unthrottled default.

micro_batch.description:
Physical forward/backward width, in tokens - llama.cpp's `n_ubatch` and
the equivalent of TRL's `per_device_train_batch_size`. This is the
activation-memory lever.

optimizer.description:
Which optimizer updates them: `"adamw"` (the default), `"sgd"`,
`"muon"` or `"gefen"`. A name this build cannot honour is refused
rather than accepted and ignored.

oneOf.description:
Physical completion fanout for differentiable shared-prefix training:
"auto", "off", "max", or an integer >= 2.

trainable.description:
Which family of parameters this run trains: `"lora"` (the default),
`"full"`, `"partial"` or `"hybrid"`. See `retrograd_core::TrainablePolicy`.

TrajectoryOverview.description:
`GET /v1/runs/{id}/trajectories`

A run without `[observe]` answers too, with `observed: false` and nothing
listed: it exists, and the answer is that it exports no trajectories.

every.description: One update in `every` exports its texts; every update has a summary.

segments.description: How many times the run started or resumed in this export.

skipped.description:
Lines and batches of the file that could not be read. Batches the run
dropped because the disk was slow are counted by the run's metric
`observe/dropped_batches`, not here.

updates.description: Every update in view, by update number.

TruncationPolicy.description:
What becomes of a member that ran out of budget mid-response.

Neither branch is free. A partial response cannot be judged as a completed
trajectory, so `Drop` is the honest reading of the reward - but dropping is a
selection on length: the model never receives a negative signal for
overrunning, and a task that systematically overruns disappears from the
gradient entirely rather than being learned out of. `MinReward` keeps the
member at the bottom of its own group, which makes overrunning cost
something at the price of a reward nobody measured.

Watch `agent/truncated_fraction` before switching: past roughly 20% the
training distribution is no longer the one the scenarios describe, and that
is the point at which the trade above stops being academic.

UpdateDetail.description:
`GET /v1/runs/{id}/trajectories/updates/{update}`: the groups of one
update, members without their texts.

groups.description: Empty for an update whose texts were not exported.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page of groups.

UpdateSummary.description: One update of a trajectory export.

metrics.description: The scalars the update published, by metric name.

segment.description: The run segment that wrote it: a resume starts a new one.

status.description: `completed` | `skipped`; absent until the update is over.

texts.description: Whether the texts of this update were exported (`every`).

trained_fraction.description: Share of the rollouts an `outcome` confirmed trained.
